The bot closes a leg by buying it back. The reason is shown with the numbers that fired it: take-profit, roll, stop-loss, delta exit, shed, manual close and others. Realized P&L is booked at each close, after fees.

A close turns open P&L into realized P&L and ends that leg's risk.

chunks.title: created
chunks.text:
When the person was added to the monitor.

Users page (admins only). The date and time the person's account was created, by an admin or, for the first admin, at the monitor's first start.

None.

chunks.title: daily swing
chunks.text:
How far the coin typically moves in one day, from DVOL: DVOL ÷ √365.

DVOL is the market's expected yearly swing of the coin. Divided by √365 it gives a typical day's swing, one daily standard deviation. With DVOL 50 that is about 2.6 %. The worst-case page shows days of 2 and 3 typical swings each way.

Bigger swings cost a short-option book money in either direction; quiet days pay it a little.

chunks.title: delta
chunks.text:
Roughly the chance an option ends up paying out, from 0 to 1.

Delta shows how much an option's price moves when the coin moves by 1. It is also a rough guess of the chance the option pays out at expiry. A 0.16-delta option pays out about 16 times in 100. When the price moves toward a strike, that leg's delta grows.

Selling at a higher delta brings more premium and a higher chance of a loss.

chunks.title: delta drift
chunks.text:
Buying back a leg whose delta fell below 0.10: far from the price, little premium left.

When the price moves away from a leg, its delta falls and little premium is left to earn. Below 0.10 the bot buys it back and repairs it at once with a fresh leg near the target delta, on the same expiry.

It replaces a leg that earns almost nothing with one that earns more, and adds that new leg's risk.

chunks.title: delta exit
chunks.text:
Closing a leg early when its delta reaches 0.30: the move against it is real.

When the price moves toward a sold strike, that leg's delta grows. At 0.30 the bot buys the leg back before it reaches the 2 times stop-loss. Afterwards the side is held like after a stop-loss.

It takes smaller losses earlier, and more of them, instead of fewer larger stop-losses.

chunks.title: delta_drift_threshold
chunks.text:
Setting: buy back a leg whose delta falls below this (0.10 shipped) and sell a fresh one.

Setting: when a leg's delta falls below this, it is far from the price with little premium left. The bot buys it back and sells a new leg at the target delta. It must be at most 75 % of every entry delta.

Up: refreshes legs sooner, more trades and fees. Down: lets legs drift further and earn less.

chunks.title: delta_exit_threshold
chunks.text:
Setting: close a leg early when its delta reaches this (0.30 shipped).

Setting: the delta exit. A leg whose delta reaches this is bought back before the stop-loss, then held like a stop. It must be above every entry delta.

Up: fewer early exits, more full stop-losses. Down: more early exits, smaller losses each.

chunks.title: deployment frequency
chunks.text:
How often a new build goes live: healthy mvp deploys a day, or new releases on stable a week.

Analytics page, Delivery (DORA) topic (admins only). One of the four DORA numbers. On mvp it counts each healthy deploy of main; on stable each new release, a tag promoted for the first time. A rolled-back deploy does not count. The chip is the DORA band: elite, high, medium or low.

It measures how the team ships changes to the bots, not how the bots trade.

chunks.title: detail
chunks.text:
Every other field of the audit line, as stored: for example the positions closed and the bot's answer.

Audit page (admins only). The rest of the line, key=value, unchanged: a close's position ids and status, a rebalance's dry run, a role change's from and to, an IP. Never a password, hash or token: the trail holds none.

None.

chunks.title: dte
chunks.text:
Days to expiry: how many whole days an option has left.

DTE counts the full days until the option's expiry date, rounded down. The bot opens positions about 25 to 50 days out and closes them when 15 days or fewer are left. The same count is used for opening and for closing.

More days left means more premium and more time for a big move; fewer days left means faster decay and sharper swings.

chunks.title: dte_delta_matrix
chunks.text:
Setting: the slots, each a target number of days and a target delta.

Setting: the list of slots. Each line names a target number of days to expiry and one or more deltas; each pair is one strangle slot. BTC ships with 25 and 50 days, ETH with 30 and 50, all at 0.16 delta.

More slots mean more positions (more income and more risk); the margin limit is split between them.

chunks.title: dte_delta_matrix.deltas
chunks.text:
Setting: the delta at which a slot sells its call and put (0.16 shipped).

Setting: the target delta for the slot's strikes. 0.16 means each leg has roughly a 16 % chance of paying out at expiry. Each delta listed is its own slot.

Higher: strikes closer to the price, more premium, more risk. Lower: further away, less premium, safer.

chunks.title: dte_delta_matrix.dte
chunks.text:
Setting: how many days to expiry a slot aims for.

Setting: the slot's target days to expiry. The bot picks the listed expiry nearest to it that no other slot holds.

Longer: more premium per trade and longer exposure. Shorter: faster decay and sharper swings.

chunks.title: dvol
chunks.text:
Deribit's index of the 30-day move the market expects for BTC or ETH.

DVOL is a volatility index published by Deribit, the exchange. It shows how big a move option prices expect over the next 30 days, as a yearly percentage. The bot uses it to set its margin limit and to size the buffer around the gamma flip.

A high DVOL means rich premiums and a market that expects large moves.

chunks.title: email
chunks.text:
A person's email address, optional, for the admin's records; the monitor sends no email.

Users page (admins only). An optional contact address an admin may record when adding a person. The monitor never sends email and never puts it in an analytics event.

None.

chunks.title: entry
chunks.text:
Selling a new strangle into an empty slot; also the price it was sold at.

An entry opens a strangle in an empty slot. The bot picks the expiry and strikes, checks each leg is worth at least the minimum premium, sizes it within the margin limit and places limit sell orders. In the positions table, 'Entry' is the price each leg was sold at.

Each entry adds premium income and the risk of a big move.

chunks.title: equity
chunks.text:
What the account is worth now: balance plus the value of open positions.

Equity is the account's value if everything were closed at current prices. 'All collateral' adds every coin, in dollars.

It rises with income and falls with losses.

chunks.title: exchange fees
chunks.text:
What Deribit charged to open and to buy back the options closed that month.

Each close carries its share of the fee paid to open the option and the fee paid to buy it back. The income page shows them as a cost; the result is already net of them.

Fees lower the income of every trade, winning or losing.

chunks.title: expiry
chunks.text:
The date an option ends.

Every option has an expiry date. After it, the option is either worth nothing or settled for its value. The bot does not hold options until expiry: it buys them back when 15 days or fewer are left, because the risk of sudden losses grows near the end.

Options with more time left pay more premium but stay exposed to price moves for longer.

chunks.title: fill timeout
chunks.text:
When an unfilled order is cancelled; the filled part is kept.

Each sell order has a time limit. When it ends, the bot cancels the rest, reads back what filled and keeps it. A strangle with only one leg filled is completed later by a repair.

None by itself: it ends the wait for a fill.

chunks.title: filled
chunks.text:
The part of an order that traded; for a sale, the part that opened a position.

An order can fill in full, in part, or not at all. The bot always records exactly what filled, never the amount it asked for. 'Opened' in the feed is a sale that filled.

Each filled sale adds premium income and risk.

chunks.title: first answers
chunks.text:
The share of new people who saw the four main answers (holding, income, worst case, last action) in their first visit.

Analytics page (admins only). A new person's first visit counts when it reaches the four answers the Overview gives: what is held, what it earned, the worst case and the last action. The card shows how many did and their share of all first visits that week.

A low share means new people miss the risk figures, not that the bots did anything.

chunks.title: flip buffer
chunks.text:
The distance from the gamma flip that counts as a real move: 1.5 normal days of price change.

The buffer is a margin around the gamma flip so that small moves do not trigger a shed. It is 1.5 times a normal day's move, taken from DVOL. A side is shed only when spot is more than this buffer beyond the flip, and sold again only when spot is back past the flip plus the buffer.

A wider buffer means fewer sheds and more exposure in a real move; a narrower one sheds more often.

chunks.title: freeze
chunks.text:
A pause on new positions while a change of volatility band or regime waits for confirmation.

When the volatility band or the gamma regime changes in a way that could lower the margin limit, the bot stops opening new positions until the change has held for 2 daily closes. Exits, rolls and repairs of rolled legs go on. If the change goes away, the freeze ends.

During a freeze no new income is added, and no new risk is taken.

chunks.title: gamma
chunks.text:
How fast delta changes when the price moves.

Gamma measures how quickly an option's delta changes when the coin moves. Sellers of options are 'short gamma': their losses speed up in big moves, more so close to expiry. That is one reason the bot closes positions with 15 days or fewer left.

High gamma means a loss can grow fast; it is highest near expiry.

chunks.title: gamma flip
chunks.text:
The price where dealer gamma changes from positive to negative.

The gamma flip is the coin price at which the dealers' gamma exposure (GEX) changes sign. Below the flip, dealer hedging tends to make moves bigger. The bot compares spot with the flip, plus a buffer, to decide whether to shed a leg and when to sell it again.

Spot well below the flip in a negative regime is the warning that sheds a side.

chunks.title: gamma regime
chunks.text:
Whether dealer hedging is calming the market (positive) or making moves bigger (negative).

The regime is the sign of the dealers' gamma exposure (GEX). Positive: dealer hedging tends to slow the price down. Negative: it tends to push the price further the way it is going. A change must hold for 2 daily closes before the bot treats it as confirmed.

A confirmed negative regime lowers the margin limit and stops sales on the side the price runs toward.

chunks.title: gamma_flip_buffer_sd
chunks.text:
Setting: how many normal days' moves beyond the gamma flip trigger a shed (1.5 shipped).

Setting: the flip buffer, in normal daily moves taken from DVOL. A side is shed only when spot is this far beyond the gamma flip in a negative regime, and sold again once it is back past the flip plus this buffer.

Up: fewer sheds, more exposure in a real move. Down: sheds more often, gives up more income.

chunks.title: gex
chunks.text:
Gamma exposure: an estimate of how option dealers' hedging pushes the price.

GEX estimates the gamma held by option dealers, the firms on the other side of most trades. To stay neutral they buy and sell the coin as the price moves. When their gamma is negative they buy into rises and sell into falls, which makes moves bigger. The bot reads GEX every minute from Deribit's main market.

Negative GEX warns that moves may grow larger; the bot sells less and sheds the threatened side.

chunks.title: gex anchor
chunks.text:
The gamma flip and buffer saved at a shed; the shed side waits until spot is back above them.

When a side is shed, the bot saves the gamma flip and buffer of that moment. The side is sold again only when spot is above that saved flip plus its buffer on 2 snapshots, or after the regime has been non-negative for 24 hours. A later jump of the live flip does not count.

It keeps the bot from selling the same side back into a move that is still going.

chunks.title: gex wait
chunks.text:
No new positions until a fresh GEX reading arrives (after a start, or when it is over 5 minutes old).

Without a fresh GEX reading, the bot cannot tell the regime or which side is safe to sell. So it opens nothing, tops up nothing and repairs nothing until one arrives. Exits, leg balancing and the MM limit still run.

It delays income briefly to avoid selling the wrong side.

chunks.title: gex_direction
chunks.text:
Setting: what decides the threatened side in a negative regime: sma (the trend) or bias (spot vs flip).

Setting: sma uses the SMA trend; bias uses spot against the gamma flip plus the buffer. Both are recorded so they can be compared. In tests the bias shed more often and returned less than the trend.

It changes which side is shed and how often, so it changes both losses avoided and income given up.

chunks.title: greeks
chunks.text:
Delta, gamma, theta and vega: four numbers that describe how an option's price reacts.

The greeks describe an option's sensitivity: delta to the coin's price, gamma to changes in delta, theta to time, vega to implied volatility. The trade history shows them at the moment of each trade. A position's delta is the option's delta times the size, negative for a sold option.

They show where a position can lose: price (delta, gamma), time (theta) and fear (vega).

chunks.title: group by
chunks.text:
Shows open positions grouped by strategy, slot, expiry or type, with totals.

Grouping puts related legs together and adds up their P&L and greeks in the group header.

None by itself.

chunks.title: held
chunks.text:
How many days a position was open before it closed.

The time from the sale of a leg to its buy-back, in days.

None by itself.

chunks.title: help used
chunks.text:
How often people opened a tip or played a video, and how many assistant answers they marked as helpful.

Analytics page (admins only). Tips opened and videos played are counts for the week. Helped is the share of the assistant's answers that people marked as helpful, with the counts beside it.

A tip or answer explains the bot; none of them is advice to trade.

chunks.title: hold rule
chunks.text:
The rule that keeps the bot from selling a missing leg again right now.

For every one-sided strangle the monitor names the rule holding its repair: a stop hold, the regime side, a GEX anchor or shed, the MM limit, a waiting stop, no fresh GEX, a working order, an unknown order, a churn pause or the roll window.

While a rule holds, the strangle earns from one leg only.

chunks.title: holding alone
chunks.text:
What the same account would have done by just holding the coin that month.

Counted in the coin, holding neither gains nor loses, so every coin the bot earns is extra. In dollars it is the coin's price change over the month times the account's balance at the month's start, from the bot's recorded history.

It shows how much of a dollar result is the coin's own move, not the strategy.

chunks.title: im
chunks.text:
Initial margin: what the exchange holds to cover open positions, as an amount or a % of the margin balance.

Initial margin (IM) is the amount the exchange sets aside for open positions and orders. The monitor shows it in dollars and as a percentage of the margin balance. 'Proj.' is the figure without the nearest expiry. The bot sizes new positions so IM stays under its limit.

More IM in use means bigger positions: more income and more risk.

chunks.title: im limit
chunks.text:
The most initial margin the bot may use, as a % of the margin balance: 20, 35 or 50 %.

The bot picks its IM limit from the volatility band: 50 % when DVOL is high against the past year, 35 % in the middle, 20 % when it is low. In a confirmed negative regime the limit is 20 %. The monitor says which reason sets the limit now.

A higher limit allows bigger positions, so more income and bigger possible losses.

chunks.title: im over limit
chunks.text:
IM is above the limit without a limit change, for example after a withdrawal. Alert only.

When initial margin rises above the limit by more than 1.5 points and no rebalance is due, for example after a withdrawal or a price move, the bot raises an alert. It does not trade. A person decides, with a rebalance preview, whether to resize. The alert clears when IM is back under the limit.

While it lasts, the book carries more risk than the limit allows and no new positions are opened.

chunks.title: implied volatility
chunks.text:
How big a move the market expects, read from option prices.

Implied volatility (IV) is the size of the price move that option prices suggest the market expects. When IV is high, options cost more, so a seller receives more premium. High IV usually comes with fear and larger moves.

Higher implied volatility means richer premiums and, usually, more risk.

chunks.title: income over months
chunks.text:
The realised result of the months shown, after fees, and the average of the months with a close.

The total adds every month's result in the table. The average divides it by the months that had at least one close, and the line under it counts the months up and down. The % compares the total with the account's balance at the start.

One good average can hide a bad month: read it with the worst month and worst week.

chunks.title: instrument
chunks.text:
The exact option traded, named by coin, expiry, strike and type, e.g. BTC-27NOV26-90000-P.

The instrument name reads: coin, expiry date, strike price, then C for a call or P for a put. Each row of the monitor is one instrument.

None by itself.

chunks.title: iv percentile
chunks.text:
Where today's DVOL sits compared with the past year, from 0 (lowest) to 100 (highest).

The IV percentile ranks today's DVOL against the past year. 0 means it is the lowest of the year, 100 the highest. The bot uses this rank to choose how much of the account may be used as margin.

A high percentile allows a higher margin limit (more positions); a low one keeps positions small.

chunks.title: iv_margin_bands
chunks.text:
Setting: the IM limit for each volatility band: 50 %, 35 % or 20 % of the margin balance.

Setting: a list of bands. Each says: when the IV percentile is at least this, initial margin may reach this % of the margin balance. A confirmed negative regime uses the lowest band.

Higher limits mean bigger positions: more income and bigger losses in a bad move.

chunks.title: iv_margin_bands.max_im_pct
chunks.text:
Setting: the IM limit of a band, in % of the margin balance.

Setting: the most initial margin the bot may use while this band applies.

Up: larger positions. Down: smaller positions.

chunks.title: iv_margin_bands.min_iv_pct
chunks.text:
Setting: the lowest IV percentile at which a band applies.

Setting: a band applies when the IV percentile is at or above this number (and below the next band's).

Lower thresholds reach the higher limits more often.

chunks.title: kill switch
chunks.text:
The emergency stop: cancel every order, buy back every position at market, stop trading.

The kill switch is an operator signal. The bot cancels all orders, books what had filled, buys back every position the exchange reports at market and checks the account is flat. Then it stays idle until a person restarts it.

It ends all risk and all income at once, at market prices.

chunks.title: last sign-in
chunks.text:
When the person last signed in with their password; never if they have not yet.

Users page (admins only). The time of the person's last successful sign-in. A browser that stays signed in refreshes its session without a new sign-in, so this can be older than their last visit.

None: an old or missing sign-in helps spot accounts nobody uses, which an admin may delete.

chunks.title: lead time
chunks.text:
How long a merged change takes to go live: the median time from a PR's merge to the first deploy that carries it.

Analytics page, Delivery (DORA) topic (admins only). One of the four DORA numbers. On mvp a change usually goes live minutes after its merge. On stable it waits for the 3-day soak on mvp and a release, so days. Below three PRs the chip says NOT YET.

A longer wait on stable is deliberate: a change runs on the test account for days before it reaches production.

chunks.title: leg
chunks.text:
One option inside a strangle: its call or its put.

A strangle has two legs, a call and a put. Each leg is managed on its own: it can be bought back, stopped out or re-sold without touching the other. A strangle with only one leg is one-sided, and the bot tries to sell the missing leg again later.

Two legs of the same size balance each other; a single leg leaves the position exposed to one direction.

chunks.title: limit price
chunks.text:
The price set on an order: it fills at that price or better, or not at all.

A limit order names its price. A sell limit fills only at that price or higher. The bot uses limit orders for entries and repairs so it never sells for less than it chose.

A higher limit means more premium if it fills, and a smaller chance it fills.

chunks.title: liquidity cap
chunks.text:
The most a new sell order may be: a small share of each strike's open interest on Deribit's main exchange.

Each entry or top-up order is capped at 10 % of each sold strike's open interest on Deribit's main exchange, and both legs get the smaller size. A strike too thin for one lot gets no order, and the slot stays short. Repairs, exits and stops are not capped.

It keeps orders to a size the market can take, at the cost of income when a slot stays short of its share.

chunks.title: manual close
chunks.text:
A person buys a leg back at market from the monitor, allowed only on the side the bot no longer sells.

The Close button buys a leg back at market. It works only while a confirmed negative regime blocks that leg's side. A confirmation window shows the cost and what follows. Afterwards the side is held like after a stop-loss.

It removes that leg's risk and income, and pays the asking price and a fee.

chunks.title: margin
chunks.text:
Money the exchange sets aside from the account to cover the risk of open positions.

Sold options can lose more than the premium, so the exchange holds part of the account as margin. Initial margin (IM) is what is needed to open positions. Maintenance margin (MM) is the floor: if it reaches 100 % of the margin balance, the exchange closes positions by force.

More margin in use means more positions, more income and more risk.

chunks.title: margin balance
chunks.text:
The money in the account that counts toward margin.

The margin balance is the account's value that the exchange counts against margin needs. The bot's limits are percentages of it: the IM limit and the MM limit. A deposit raises it and a withdrawal lowers it.

A larger margin balance lets the bot hold larger positions within the same percentage limits.

chunks.title: mark
chunks.text:
The price used to value an open leg: the middle of the live bid and ask.

The mark is the price at which the bot values a leg, from the exchange's live quote. Without a live quote it keeps the last known mark and says so. Unrealized P&L and the stop-loss use the mark.

A rising mark on a sold option is a growing loss.

chunks.title: max_leg_size_multiple
chunks.text:
Setting: a new leg is at most this many times its slot's normal size (2 shipped).

Setting: the normal size is the slot's margin share divided by one strangle's own margin. Margin that nets positions can make a leg look almost free; this cap stops that from inflating sizes.

Up: bigger positions when margin allows. Down: smaller, steadier positions.

chunks.title: max_mm_pct
chunks.text:
Setting: the MM limit. At this % of the margin balance the bot buys positions back (35 shipped).

Setting: when maintenance margin reaches this % of the margin balance, the bot buys back positions at market and opens nothing until it is back under. Deribit liquidates at 100 %.

Up: closer to liquidation before acting. Down: earlier forced reductions.

chunks.title: min_premium
chunks.text:
Setting: the smallest premium per leg worth selling, in the coin (0.001 shipped).

Setting: a leg is sold only if its premium, at the lowest price the bot may lower to, is at least this. 0 accepts any premium.

Up: fewer, richer trades. Down: more trades for smaller premiums, with the same tail risk.

chunks.title: missing leg
chunks.text:
The leg a one-sided strangle lacks, and the rule keeping the bot from selling it again.

When a leg is closed, its strangle keeps only the other leg. The bot sells the missing leg again (a repair) when it is safe. The monitor shows each missing leg and the rule that holds it now, such as a cooldown after a stop-loss.

While a leg is missing the position earns less and leans to one side.

chunks.title: mm
chunks.text:
Maintenance margin: the floor. At 100 % of the margin balance the exchange closes positions by force.

Maintenance margin (MM) is the least the account must keep to hold its positions. If MM reaches 100 % of the margin balance, the exchange liquidates, meaning it closes positions at market. The bot cuts positions itself long before that, at 35 %.

MM is the distance to liquidation: the higher it is, the closer a forced close.

chunks.title: mm limit
chunks.text:
If maintenance margin reaches 35 % of the margin balance, the bot buys positions back at once.

The MM limit is the bot's own safety line, far from the exchange's 100 %. When maintenance margin reaches it, the bot buys back positions at market right away and blocks new sales and repairs until margin is back under it.

It trades some income and fees for a wide distance from a forced liquidation.

chunks.title: moneyness
chunks.text:
Whether a strike is at, away from, or past today's price (ATM, OTM, ITM).

Moneyness compares a strike with the current price. OTM (out of the money) means the option would pay nothing today. ATM (at the money) means the strike is about at the price. ITM (in the money) means the option would pay something today. The bot sells OTM options.

A sold option moving from OTM toward ITM is losing money.

chunks.title: month
chunks.text:
A calendar month in UTC.

Income is summed per month in UTC; a month without closes says so.

None.

chunks.title: nps
chunks.text:
Net Promoter Score: the share of people who would recommend the monitor (9–10) minus the share who would not (0–6).

Analytics page (admins only). Once a month the assistant asks how likely a person is to recommend the monitor, from 0 to 10. Promoters answer 9–10, passives 7–8 and detractors 0–6. The score runs from −100 to +100 and is shown only once enough people have answered.

It measures how people feel about the monitor, not how the bots trade.

chunks.title: option
chunks.text:
A contract that gives its buyer the right to buy or sell a coin at a set price until a set date.

An option is a contract. The buyer pays a price, the premium, up front. In return the buyer may buy (a call) or sell (a put) the coin at the strike price until the expiry date. The seller keeps the premium and must pay out if the price moves past the strike.

Selling options brings income now (the premium) in exchange for a possible payout later that can be much larger.

chunks.title: order sent
chunks.text:
An order the bot placed on the exchange.

Each order the bot places is counted and written to its journal with the market at that moment. One entry can need several orders, because unfilled orders are cancelled and tried again.

None by itself: only the filled part becomes a position.

chunks.title: p&l
chunks.text:
Profit and loss, after Deribit's fees, in US dollars or in the coin.

P&L is the profit or loss of positions, net of the exchange's fees. Realized P&L comes from closed legs; unrealized P&L is the open legs valued at the current mark. Total P&L adds both. Dollar figures use the coin's price at that moment.

It is the result of the income earned and the losses paid so far.

chunks.title: p&l %
chunks.text:
Unrealized P&L as a % of the premium received: +50 % is half the premium earned.

P&L % compares a leg's open result with its premium. +50 % means half the premium is profit, 0 % is break-even, −100 % means the loss equals the premium. The stop-loss fires near −200 % with the 2 times setting.

It shows how close a leg is to its take-profit (+50 %) or its stop-loss (about −200 %).

chunks.title: person
chunks.text:
Who did it: the username of the person who signed in, changed a user or acted on a bot.

Audit page (admins only). The username stored on the audit line. For a failed sign-in it is the name that was typed. Lines written by the monitor itself or the admin command line say system or cli.

None: it answers who closed a leg or rebalanced, without shell access.

chunks.title: position
chunks.text:
An option the account holds now, sold or bought.

A position is an open option on the account. The bot's positions are the legs of its strangles. The account can also hold positions the bot does not manage; they still use margin.

Every open position carries its own risk and income.

chunks.title: premium
chunks.text:
The price of an option. The seller receives it up front.

The premium is what the buyer pays for an option and what the seller receives. The bot is a seller, so the premium is its income. It keeps all of it if the option ends worthless, and part of it if it buys the option back for less.

A higher premium means more income per trade, but it is usually paid for more risk.

chunks.title: premium kept
chunks.text:
The share of a leg's premium the bot would keep if it bought the leg back now.

Premium kept compares the price the leg was sold at with its price now. If a leg was sold for 0.0100 and now costs 0.0060, 40 % of the premium is kept. It turns negative when the option costs more than it was sold for: that leg is at a loss.

It is the income already earned on a leg; the take-profit closes a leg once enough of it is kept.

chunks.title: price
chunks.text:
The price an option traded at, in the coin (e.g. 0.0125 BTC).

Deribit prices these options in the coin itself, not in dollars. The monitor converts to dollars at the coin's price where it says USD.

None by itself.

chunks.title: put
chunks.text:
An option that pays its buyer when the coin falls below the strike price.

A put option gives its buyer the right to sell the coin at the strike price. It gains value when the coin falls below the strike. The bot sells puts: it keeps the premium if the coin stays above the strike, and loses when the coin falls far below it.

A sold put earns its premium in a flat or rising market and loses money in a sharp fall.

chunks.title: quantity
chunks.text:
The size of a position or order, in coins of the underlying (e.g. 0.1 BTC).

Option sizes on Deribit are counted in coins of the underlying asset. A 0.1 BTC option covers a move of 0.1 BTC. The bot sizes each slot from the margin limit.

Bigger size means more premium and a bigger loss in a bad move.

chunks.title: re-priced
chunks.text:
A working order whose price the bot changed so it fills.

When a sell order does not fill, the bot lowers its price in steps: first the asking price, then the middle price, then a floor. Each change is journaled.

A lower price fills sooner and brings a little less premium.

chunks.title: realized p&l
chunks.text:
Profit or loss already locked in by closed legs, after fees.

Realized P&L is booked when a leg is bought back: the premium received minus the buy-back price, its share of the opening fees and the closing fee. It does not change after the close.

It is income (or loss) already earned; no more risk is attached to it.

chunks.title: reason
chunks.text:
Why the bot opened or closed a position, with the rule's numbers.

Every trade carries its reason, for example 'take-profit' or 'stop-loss', and the numbers that fired the rule. The same reasons group results in the history.

None by itself: it explains the trade.

chunks.title: rebalance
chunks.text:
Resizing the positions toward the current margin limit: selling more (top-up) or buying back (downsize).

When the confirmed margin limit changes, at startup, or on a person's request, the bot resizes each slot toward its share of the limit. It sells more when there is room and buys back when the book is too large. A person can preview a rebalance before running it.

A top-up adds income and risk; a downsize removes both and pays fees and the spread.

chunks.title: reconcile
chunks.text:
Loading the exchange's real positions into the bot's book, at startup or when they differ.

The exchange is the source of truth. At each start the bot reads every position the exchange holds and rebuilds its book from it. During trading, a difference that lasts 2 checks is taken into the book. 'Loaded' in the feed is such a step.

None by itself: it makes sure every real position is managed.

chunks.title: regime side
chunks.text:
The side the bot does not sell in a confirmed negative regime: puts in a bear trend, calls in a bull trend.

When the negative regime is confirmed, the side the price is running toward is not sold. New strangles open only the other leg, and repairs or top-ups of that side wait. With no trend, both sides are sold.

It keeps the bot out of the side most at risk, and keeps the income of the other side.

chunks.title: release train
chunks.text:
The last 8 days of deploys: a mark for each stable release and a tick for each mvp deploy.

Analytics page, Delivery (DORA) topic (admins only). Opening a PR in What went live puts a dot on each lane. A filled dot is where it went live; a hollow dot at the right edge means it is still waiting there.

It shows when builds changed, which helps to match a change in the bots' behaviour to a deploy.

chunks.title: repair
chunks.text:
Selling a strangle's missing leg again, at the same expiry and size.

When a strangle has lost one leg, the bot sells that leg again on the same expiry, near the original delta, with the same size. After a take-profit or a drift roll it repairs at once. After a stop-loss or a delta exit it waits 72 hours and for a calm market.

A repair restores the premium income and the balance of the strangle.

chunks.title: repair_cooldown_hours
chunks.text:
Setting: hours a stopped-out side stays empty before it may be sold again (72 shipped).

Setting: after a stop-loss, delta exit, manual close or MM cut, that side waits this many hours, and a calm market, before a repair.

Up: longer pause after a loss, less income meanwhile. Down: re-enters sooner, possibly into the same move.

chunks.title: request draft
chunks.text:
A bug report or wish the assistant writes for you to check and send, never sent on its own.

When you report a problem or ask for a change, the assistant first checks it. A request is drafted only when it says what happened, where, and shows the data behind it. Evidence lists that data: a number, a journal entry or a P&L point. Steps say how to see the problem again. You can edit the draft, then send it to a private queue.

None: a request changes nothing in the bot or the account.

chunks.title: reserved
chunks.text:
Coin set aside for open spot orders.

Money held back by orders to buy or sell the coin itself, not options.

None for the bot.

chunks.title: retention
chunks.text:
Of the people who first came in a given week, the share who came back in each of the next four weeks.

Analytics page (admins only). Each row is a group of people whose first visit fell in the same week: the first week. The columns show the share of that group seen again one, two, three and four weeks later. A dash marks a week that has not ended yet.

It measures whether the monitor is useful enough to come back to, not trading results.

chunks.title: roi_take_profit
chunks.text:
Setting: buy a leg back once this share of its premium is earned (0.50 = 50 % shipped).

Setting: the take-profit. When a leg has earned this share of its premium, the bot buys it back and sells a fresh one.

Up: holds longer for more, stays exposed longer. Down: banks sooner and trades more often.

chunks.title: role
chunks.text:
What a person may do on the monitor: user sees it, manager also closes and rebalances, admin also manages people.

Users page (admins only). Every person has one of three roles. A user sees the monitor. A manager may also close a leg by hand and rebalance. An admin may also add people, change roles, reset passwords and delete people. The server checks the role on every action. Changing it signs the person out everywhere.

A manager can send orders to the bots: give that role only to people who should.

chunks.title: rollout_dte
chunks.text:
Setting: buy a strangle back when this many days or fewer are left (15 shipped).

Setting: the time roll. When an expiry has this many days or fewer left, its legs are bought back and the slot reopens further out. Every slot's target must be above it.

Up: exits earlier, less late-expiry risk, less decay earned. Down: holds longer, more decay and more risk.

chunks.title: shed
chunks.text:
Closing the threatened side of every strangle when the market may move hard that way.

A shed buys back the side under threat: in a negative regime, with spot more than the buffer below the gamma flip and a trend, puts in a bear trend and calls in a bull trend. The signal must hold on 2 snapshots in a row. The side is sold again only once the price recovers.

A shed limits losses in a strong move but gives up that side's income until the price recovers.

chunks.title: side
chunks.text:
SELL means a sold option (premium received); BUY means a bought one (premium paid).

The bot's strangles are sold: SELL. A bought option, BUY, pays a premium, for example as insurance on a sold one. Positions the bot does not manage can be either side.

A sold option earns premium with open-ended risk; a bought one costs premium with a capped loss.

chunks.title: skipped
chunks.text:
A chance to open or resize that the bot let pass, with its reason.

When a rule says no, the bot writes down what it did not do and why, for example a premium too small, a freeze, or no fresh GEX reading. These lines show why a slot stayed empty.

A skip adds neither risk nor income.

chunks.title: slot
chunks.text:
A place the bot keeps for one strangle, set by a number of days and a delta.

The settings list slots such as 'a strangle about 25 days out at 0.16 delta'. Each slot holds one strangle at a time and gets an equal share of the margin limit. When a slot is empty, the bot opens a new strangle in it.

More slots spread the money over more positions; fewer slots put more in each one.

chunks.title: sma trend
chunks.text:
The price trend (bull, bear or neutral) read from the 9-day and 21-day moving averages.

A moving average (SMA) is the average closing price of the last days. The bot compares the 9-day and 21-day averages and recent highs and lows to call the trend bull, bear or neutral. In a negative regime, the trend says which side is threatened.

The trend decides which side the bot stops selling in a negative regime: puts in a bear trend, calls in a bull trend.

chunks.title: soak
chunks.text:
The 3 days a build runs on mvp, the test account, before it may be released to stable.

Analytics page, Delivery (DORA) topic (admins only). A release goes on the newest mvp deploy that is at least 3 days old. Until then a PR's stable column says when its soak ends, then that it waits for the next release.

The soak lets a change prove itself on the test account before it reaches production capital.

chunks.title: spot
chunks.text:
Today's price of the coin.

Spot is the current market price of BTC or ETH. Every other number on the monitor is measured against it: how far a strike is, how far the gamma flip is, and the value of positions in US dollars.

Spot moving toward a strike raises the risk of that leg.

chunks.title: stop hold
chunks.text:
After a stop-loss, delta exit or manual close, that side is not sold again for 72 hours.

A leg closed by a stop-loss, a delta exit, a manual close or the MM limit is held. It is sold again only after 72 hours, with no freeze and no confirmed negative regime. The hold survives restarts. 'Cooldown until' shows when the 72 hours end.

It avoids selling into the same move that caused the loss, at the cost of income while the side is empty.

chunks.title: stop waiting
chunks.text:
A stop-loss waiting up to 5 minutes because the order book is nearly empty.

When a stop-loss triggers but the asking price is more than 20 % above the middle price, sellers have left the order book, as in a flash crash. The bot waits and checks each cycle. It buys back once prices are normal, or at market after 5 minutes. Meanwhile no new positions are opened.

It avoids paying a panic price for a buy-back, and adds up to 5 minutes of exposure.

chunks.title: stop-loss
chunks.text:
Buying a leg back at market when its loss reaches 2 times the premium received.

The stop-loss is the first exit rule. When a leg's loss reaches the set multiple of its premium (2 times), the bot buys it back at market, ahead of everything else. 'Stop @' is the option price at which that happens. If the order book is empty it waits up to 5 minutes.

It caps the loss on most moves; a sudden gap can still go past it.

chunks.title: stop_loss_multiplier
chunks.text:
Setting: buy a leg back at market when its loss reaches this many times its premium (2 shipped).

Setting: the stop-loss. A leg is bought back at market when its loss reaches this multiple of the premium received for it.

Up: fewer stop-outs, bigger losses each. Down: more stop-outs, smaller losses each.

chunks.title: strangle
chunks.text:
One call sold above today's price and one put sold below it, with the same expiry.

A short strangle sells a call above the current price and a put below it, both ending on the same date. The seller keeps the premium if the coin stays between the two strikes. A big move either way causes a loss, and that loss has no cap.

It earns the premium of both options in a calm market and loses in a big move in either direction.

chunks.title: strategy
chunks.text:
The set of rules a bot trades by; here, short strangles.

The strategy names the trading plan, for example short strangles. The monitor can filter and group by it.

None by itself.

chunks.title: strategy_id
chunks.text:
Setting: the strategy's name in the bot's journal and order labels.

A name for the strategy, written on every journal line and order label so trades can be traced. It does not change how the bot trades.

None.

chunks.title: strike
chunks.text:
The fixed price written in an option contract.

The strike is the price at which the option's buyer may buy (call) or sell (put) the coin. For the bot, a strike far from today's price is safer but pays a smaller premium. A strike close to today's price pays more and is more likely to be reached.

Strikes closer to the price bring more income and more risk; strikes further away bring less of both.

chunks.title: take-profit
chunks.text:
Buying a leg back once 50 % of its premium has been earned.

When a leg's buy-back price has fallen to half of what it was sold for, the bot buys it back and keeps the gain. It first rests an order at the middle price, then crosses to the asking price. The missing leg is then sold again at once.

It banks part of the premium early instead of holding for all of it.

chunks.title: target / bot
chunks.text:
What the action was done to: the person whose account changed, or the bot that was asked to close or rebalance.

Audit page (admins only). For a user change it is the person changed. For a manual close or rebalance it is the bot. Empty for sign-ins and sign-outs.

None.

chunks.title: theta
chunks.text:
Time decay: how much value an option loses each day.

Theta is the amount an option's price drops each day if nothing else changes. An option seller earns this decay. It speeds up in the last weeks before expiry.

Theta is the seller's daily income from time passing; it does not protect against a big price move.

chunks.title: time
chunks.text:
When something happened, in São Paulo time (BRT).

The time of a trade or event. The bot records times in UTC; the monitor shows them in São Paulo time, marked BRT.

None.

chunks.title: time roll
chunks.text:
Buying a strangle back when 15 days or fewer are left before expiry.

Losses can grow fastest in the last weeks before expiry. When 15 days or fewer are left, the bot buys the strangle's legs back. Once both are gone, the slot opens a new strangle further out.

It gives up the last weeks of decay to avoid the sharpest swings.

chunks.title: time to restore
chunks.text:
How long a failure lasted: from the failed deploy to the healthy deploy or fix that ended it, median.

Analytics page, Delivery (DORA) topic (admins only). One of the four DORA numbers. A rollback usually restores within minutes; a bug lasts until its fix goes live. NO FAILURE means there was nothing to restore that week.

While a failure lasts the bot may run an older or a faulty build: a short time to restore limits that.

chunks.title: underlying
chunks.text:
The coin this bot trades options on: BTC or ETH.

Setting: the coin whose options the bot sells. Each bot trades one coin, on its own account. Prices, premiums and the minimum premium are in this coin.

Each coin has its own volatility: ETH usually moves more than BTC.

chunks.title: unknown order
chunks.text:
An order that may or may not have reached the exchange; the bot cancels it before acting again.

If the connection drops while an order is sent, the bot cannot know whether the exchange took it. It cancels the order by its label every cycle until that succeeds, and blocks that slot meanwhile. Any position that turns up is then taken into the book.

It prevents a double position; the slot earns nothing new while it waits.

chunks.title: unrealized p&l
chunks.text:
Profit or loss of open legs if they were bought back now at the mark, after opening fees.

Unrealized P&L is the premium received minus what it would cost to buy the open legs back at the current mark, minus the fees paid to open. It changes with every price move until the leg is closed.

It can still change a lot: a profit on paper is not yet income.

chunks.title: usd
chunks.text:
US dollars, at the coin's price at that moment.

The bot earns in the coin. Dollar figures convert at the coin's price at each close, or today's price for open positions.

None by itself; the coin's own price changes dollar figures.

chunks.title: username
chunks.text:
The name a person signs in to the monitor with: 3 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, dot, underscore or hyphen.

Users page (admins only). The name a person types to sign in. It is not case-sensitive and two people cannot share one. An admin chooses it when adding the person.

None: it only identifies who signed in and who acted, in the audit trail.

chunks.title: vega
chunks.text:
How much an option's price changes when implied volatility changes by 1 point.

Vega measures how sensitive an option's price is to implied volatility, the size of move the market expects. When fear rises, implied volatility rises and sold options cost more to buy back, even if the price has not moved.

A seller loses on paper when implied volatility rises and gains when it falls.

chunks.title: what went live
chunks.text:
Every merged pull request, with its merge time and when it went live on mvp and on stable.

Analytics page, Delivery (DORA) topic (admins only). One row per merged PR, newest first. PR is its number, Epic the product area it belongs to. Merged is when it joined main. The two live columns say when the first deploy that carried it went live. Delivery result is ROLLED BACK, ON STABLE, LIVE ON MVP or NOT LIVE.

It lists changes to the bots' code; a row says nothing about the bots' results.

chunks.title: win / loss size
chunks.text:
Average win divided by average loss.

Below 1 means a typical loss is bigger than a typical win, which is normal for option selling. Read it together with the win rate.

A lower ratio needs a higher win rate to break even.

chunks.title: win rate
chunks.text:
The share of closes that made money.

Win rate counts closes with a positive result after fees. A high win rate is normal for option selling and does not tell you the size of the losses: compare it with the average win and loss.

A high win rate can sit beside rare large losses.

chunks.title: withdrawable
chunks.text:
How much can be taken out of the account now.

The amount the exchange would let you withdraw without breaking margin needs.

Withdrawing lowers the margin balance, which can push IM over the limit.

chunks.title: working order
chunks.text:
An order on the exchange that has not filled yet.

The bot sells with limit orders, which wait on the exchange until a buyer accepts the price. While an order works, the bot lowers its price a few times. After the fill timeout it cancels the rest and keeps whatever filled.

A working order adds risk only as it fills.

chunks.title: worst case
chunks.text:
A model of what one very bad day would cost the open positions: a fall or rise of 3 typical daily swings.

The bot reprices each open leg with Black–Scholes on its own implied volatility after one day, with the coin 3 daily standard deviations lower and higher (from DVOL). The tile shows the worse side in the coin, in dollars and as a % of the account. It is a model, not a quote.

Real days can move more than 3 swings, so a loss can be larger than this figure.

chunks.title: worst month
chunks.text:
The month with the lowest realised result, after fees.

Among the months with at least one close, the one that earned least or lost most. Under it, the coin's recorded price move that month, when the bot's history has it.

It shows the size of a bad month, which an average hides.

chunks.title: worst week
chunks.text:
The lowest change of the bot's total P&L over any 7 days, with its dates.

Taken from the bot's P&L history, open positions included, in the coin and as a % of the account's balance at the start. Days without history are listed, never filled in.

It is the drop an investor would have lived through in one week.

chunks.title: cancelled:gamma_close
chunks.text: Cancelled the order to sell the option: market makers' positioning turned against that side. Nothing had filled.

chunks.title: cancelled:kill_switch
chunks.text: Cancelled the order to sell the option: the kill switch stopped all trading. Nothing had filled.

chunks.title: cancelled:order_timeout
chunks.text: Cancelled the order to sell the option: it did not fill within the time allowed. Nothing had filled. If only one side of a strangle filled, a repair sells the other side later.

chunks.title: cancelled:regime_side
chunks.text: Cancelled the order to sell the option: market makers amplify moves now and the trend turned toward that side, so it is not sold. Nothing had filled.

chunks.title: cancelled:resting_close
chunks.text: Cancelled the resting order to buy back the option. Nothing had filled. If the rule that sent it still applies, the rest is bought at the asking price.

chunks.title: cancelled:risk_frozen
chunks.text: Cancelled the order to sell the option: new risk was paused (a margin-limit change waits for confirmation, or maintenance margin is too high). Nothing had filled.

chunks.title: closed:delta_drift
chunks.text: Bought back the option: little premium was left to earn; it is sold again nearer the price (delta drift)

chunks.title: closed:delta_exit
chunks.text: Bought back the option: the price moved close to its strike, so the risk grew too fast (delta exit). Like a stop-loss, it will not be sold again on that side until its cooldown ends

chunks.title: closed:dte_rollout
chunks.text: Bought back the option: only few days to expiry left, so the strangle closes before expiry (time roll). The slot then opens a new strangle on a later expiry

chunks.title: closed:gamma_regime
chunks.text: Bought back the option: market makers' positioning pointed to a strong move against it (GEX shed). It is sold again once that signal has passed

chunks.title: closed:kill_switch
chunks.text: Bought back the option: the kill switch closed every position. The bot stays idle until it is restarted

chunks.title: closed:manual_close
chunks.text: Bought back the option by hand from the monitor (manual close). Like a stop-loss, it will not be sold again on that side until its cooldown ends

chunks.title: closed:margin_mm_limit
chunks.text: Bought back part of the option: maintenance margin reached its safety limit (margin cut). Nothing new is sold until it is lower

chunks.title: closed:rebalance_downsize
chunks.text: Bought back part of the option: margin in use was above its limit (rebalance). The rest stays open

chunks.title: closed:rebalance_legs
chunks.text: Bought back the extra option so the call and the put are the same size (leg balance)

chunks.title: closed:roi_target
chunks.text: Bought back the option: most of its premium was already earned (take-profit). The option is sold again to complete the strangle

chunks.title: closed:stop_loss
chunks.text: Bought back the option: it lost twice its premium (stop-loss). It was bought back to limit the loss; the option will not be sold again on that side until its cooldown ends

chunks.title: config_loaded:first
chunks.text: The bot recorded the settings it trades with; later starts will say what changed.

chunks.title: config_loaded:unchanged
chunks.text: The bot restarted with the same settings as before.

chunks.title: filled:entry
chunks.text: Sold the option to open a new strangle and collect its premium (entry)

chunks.title: filled:rebalance_upsize
chunks.text: Sold more of the option to bring the slot up to its share of the margin limit (rebalance)

chunks.title: filled:repair
chunks.text: Sold the option again to complete its strangle (repair)

chunks.title: key_scope:can_move_funds
chunks.text: The bot checked its exchange key at startup: the key can also move funds out of the account. The policy refuses withdrawal rights, so the key should be replaced by a trade-only one; the bot keeps trading meanwhile.

chunks.title: key_scope:trade_only
chunks.text: The bot checked its exchange key at startup: it can trade but cannot withdraw or transfer funds.

chunks.title: key_scope:unknown
chunks.text: The bot could not read what its exchange key may do at startup, so whether it can move funds is unknown.

chunks.title: pnl
chunks.text: A periodic profit-and-loss snapshot; nothing was traded.

chunks.title: reconciled
chunks.text: Found a short option on the exchange at startup and took it into the book; the bot manages it like a position it sold itself.

chunks.title: risk_limit:frozen
chunks.text: New risk is paused: a change in volatility or in market makers' positioning would lower the margin limit, and it waits to be confirmed on daily closes. Exits, rolls and repairs continue.

chunks.title: risk_limit:im_over_limit
chunks.text: Margin in use (N %) is above its limit (N %) with no rebalance due, for example after a transfer or a price move. This is an alert only: the bot sends no order for it.

chunks.title: risk_limit:im_over_limit_cleared
chunks.text: Margin in use is back at or under its limit; the alert ends.

chunks.title: risk_limit:im_under_use
chunks.text: Margin in use (N %) has stayed under 60 % of its limit (N %) for hours while new trades were allowed. This is an alert only: the bot sends no order for it.

chunks.title: risk_limit:im_under_use_cleared
chunks.text: The unused-margin alert ends: margin in use is back at 60 % of its limit or more, or new trades are no longer allowed.

chunks.title: risk_limit:limit_changed
chunks.text: The margin limit changed to N % of the margin balance after a confirmed change in volatility or market positioning. The positions are resized toward it.

chunks.title: risk_limit:mm_breach
chunks.text: Maintenance margin reached its safety limit: positions are bought back at market now, and nothing new is sold until it is lower.

chunks.title: risk_limit:rebalance
chunks.text: The positions are resized so the margin in use matches the limit: slots under their share get more, slots over it are bought back in part.

chunks.title: risk_limit:rebalance_in_band
chunks.text: After a restart the positions were left as they are: the margin in use is already close to its limit.

chunks.title: risk_limit:rebalance_manual
chunks.text: A person asked for a rebalance from the monitor: the positions are resized toward the margin limit.

chunks.title: risk_limit:rebalance_retry
chunks.text: A rebalance order did not fill in full. The bot tries again after a short wait.

chunks.title: risk_limit:regime_seeded
chunks.text: First start with no history: the bot took today's market positioning as confirmed, so it trades from the start.

chunks.title: risk_limit:unfrozen
chunks.text: New risk is allowed again: the change that paused it was confirmed or went away.

chunks.title: skipped:bias_warmup
chunks.text: A close of one side was held back: that signal is trusted only once a full hour of data supports it (after a restart or a data gap). New sales of that side wait meanwhile.

chunks.title: skipped:churn_paused
chunks.text: This slot is paused: it bought back and sold again too many times within an hour. It resumes when the pause ends; exits still run.

chunks.title: skipped:entry_rejected
chunks.text: No new strangle in this slot: the order could not be sent (premium too small, size under the minimum, or an exchange error). It tries again next cycle.

chunks.title: skipped:entry_wait_topup
chunks.text: No new strangle yet: a rebalance order is still working, and the bot sizes one new position at a time so the two do not add up past the margin limit.

chunks.title: skipped:gex_wait
chunks.text: No new risk yet: the market makers' positioning data (GEX) is missing or out of date, so the bot waits for a fresh reading.

chunks.title: skipped:liquidity_cap
chunks.text: The order was made smaller: it is kept to a small share of the contracts open on each strike, so it can fill without moving the price. Under one contract nothing is sent.

chunks.title: skipped:manual_close_refused
chunks.text: A manual close from the monitor was refused: it is allowed only on a side the bot no longer sells (a negative gamma regime with the trend moving toward that side). Nothing was bought.

chunks.title: skipped:margin_limit
chunks.text: No new strangle in this slot: the margin it would use does not fit under the margin limit. The slot is tried again each cycle.

chunks.title: skipped:margin_unknown
chunks.text: No new strangle: the exchange's margin figures are missing or out of date, so the bot adds no risk until they come back.

chunks.title: skipped:no_expiry
chunks.text: No new strangle in this slot: the exchange lists no expiry date in the slot's range. It waits for one.

chunks.title: skipped:no_free_expiry
chunks.text: No new strangle in this slot: every expiry date in its range is already used by another slot, and each slot keeps its own date. It waits for a free one.

chunks.title: skipped:no_strike
chunks.text: No new option sold in this slot: no strike price was close enough to the slot's target risk (delta) with a real market — a buyer and a seller, and a price in line with the options near the money. It tries again next cycle.

chunks.title: skipped:rebalance_wait_entry
chunks.text: The rebalance waits: an entry order is still working, and the bot sizes one new position at a time so the two do not add up past the margin limit.

chunks.title: skipped:regime_side
chunks.text: One side is not sold: market makers' positioning favours strong moves and the price trend runs toward that side, so the bot sells only the other side for now.

chunks.title: skipped:repair_held
chunks.text: A missing leg is not sold again yet: a rule still holds that side back (a cooldown after a stop-loss or a close by hand, a GEX shed whose signal has not passed, or the trend under a negative gamma regime). It is sold again once that rule lets it go.

chunks.title: skipped:repair_held:gex_shed
chunks.text: A missing leg is not sold again yet: it was bought back because market makers' positioning pointed to a strong move against it (GEX shed). It is sold again once that signal has passed for long enough, not on a single reading.

chunks.title: skipped:repair_held:regime_side
chunks.text: A missing leg is not sold again yet: market makers' positioning favours strong moves and the price trend runs toward that side, so the bot does not sell it until that changes.

chunks.title: skipped:repair_held:stopped
chunks.text: A missing leg is not sold again yet: that side was closed by a stop-loss, a quick exit, a margin cut or by hand, so the bot waits for its cooldown and a calmer market before selling it again.

chunks.title: skipped:repair_held:stopped_top_up
chunks.text: The rebalance adds nothing to this slot yet: one of its sides was closed by a stop-loss, a quick exit, a margin cut or by hand, and that side waits for its cooldown and a calmer market. The rebalance tries again later.

chunks.title: skipped:risk_frozen
chunks.text: No new strangle: new risk is paused while a change in volatility or in market makers' positioning waits to be confirmed on daily closes. Exits and repairs continue.

chunks.title: skipped:stop_deferred
chunks.text: A stop-loss waits a few minutes: the option's order book is too thin (the asking price is far above the mid), so buying at market would cost too much. It fires once the spread is normal, or at market when the wait ends; nothing new is sold meanwhile.

chunks.title: submitted:close_long
chunks.text: Sent an order to sell the option because the bot held it long, and the strategy only sells options. It sells at the best bid.

chunks.title: submitted:entry
chunks.text: Sent an order to sell the option to open a new strangle and collect its premium. It rests on the order book; if it does not fill, its price steps down and it is cancelled after the fill timeout.

chunks.title: submitted:rebalance_upsize
chunks.text: Sent an order to sell the option to bring the slot up to its share of the margin limit. It rests on the order book; if it does not fill, its price steps down and it is cancelled after the fill timeout.

chunks.title: submitted:repair
chunks.text: Sent an order to sell the option to complete its strangle again. It rests on the order book; if it does not fill, its price steps down and it is cancelled after the fill timeout.

chunks.title: submitted:rollout_19dte
chunks.text: Sent an order to buy back the option because it is close to expiry. It rests at the mid price for a while; if the rule still applies when that time ends, the rest is bought at the asking price.

chunks.title: submitted:rollout_delta_drift
chunks.text: Sent an order to buy back the option because little premium is left to earn. It rests at the mid price for a while; if the rule still applies when that time ends, the rest is bought at the asking price.

chunks.title: submitted:rollout_roi
chunks.text: Sent an order to buy back the option because most of its premium is already earned. It rests at the mid price for a while; if the rule still applies when that time ends, the rest is bought at the asking price.
